subject: Clarifying commit tiers, minimum spend & overage/burst terms for Hosted API
messages:
From: Sylvia Kim <sylvia@paymentsinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API commit / overage questions

Hi Marissa / Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week — Payments Inc. liked the latency profile and the model routing features. Before we move to procurement, legal wants some specifics about the financials for the Hosted API. A few questions we need clarified so we can prepare an SOW: 

- Minimum monthly/annual commit: what are your standard minimums per tier? Can we structure a lower entry-level commit for a pilot?
- On-demand over commit: how is the overage rate calculated? Are overages charged at list on-demand, or at a multiplier of the commit per-token price?
- Burst pricing: what happens when we exceed commit temporarily (e.g., 2x traffic for a few hours)? Is there an automated buffer or burst bucket? Any penalties?
- True-up / smoothing: do you allow monthly smoothing against an annual commit, or is each month measured independently?

I've attached our procurement requirements and the internal billing policy. Legal also asked for an example calculation (we want to see a worked example: commit size, price per token, on-demand multiplier, and final monthly charge for a spike month).

Can you send a one-page term sheet and an example calc? If possible we’d like to finalize commercial terms this week.

Thanks,

--
Sylvia Kim
Head of Platform
Payments Inc.
procurement_requirements.pdf (attached)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Kim <sylvia@paymentsinc.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Hosted API commit / overage questions

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a short proposal attached.

Summary (high level):
- Minimums: Standard entry commit is 1M tokens/month, but we can offer a short pilot at 250k tokens/month for 3 months (see proposal).
- Overage: Overage is charged at a multiplier on the committed per-token rate, not public list-rate. Standard multiplier is 1.5x the commit per-token price.
- Burst: We provide a burst buffer equal to 25% of committed tokens available per month by default; bursts beyond that are billed at the overage multiplier. We can add one monthly free spike event (up to 50% extra) for the first quarter.
- Smoothing / true-up: We support annual commits with monthly smoothing (true-up at quarter / year-end). Contracts can be monthly or annual.

Attached: Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf (one-page term sheet + worked examples). Highlights from the attached: 
- Commit tiers and per-token commit price (examples):
  • 250k/mo — $0.0006 / token (pilot)
  • 1M/mo — $0.00045 / token
  • 5M/mo — $0.00033 / token
  • 20M+/mo — custom pricing (contact AE)
- Overage rate = commit_price * 1.5 (billed per extra token)
- Burst behavior: automatic prefix/KV caching reduces tokens billed in many spikes; in addition, monthly burst buffer (25%) is included. Bursts beyond buffer billed at overage rate.
- Example calc (worked example in PDF):
  • Commit: 1M tokens @ $0.00045 = $450/month
  • Usage month: 1.6M tokens (includes a spike)
  • Included burst buffer: 250k tokens (25%) -> billed as committed
  • Overage: 350k tokens @ $0.00045*1.5 = $0.000675 -> $236.25
  • Total month charge: $450 + $236.25 = $686.25

Questions we have for you to finalize:
1) Would Payments Inc. be comfortable with an annual commit with quarterly true-ups, or do you need month-to-month?
2) For pre-prod/dev traffic, do you want that metered against the same commit or on a separate non-committed on-demand meter? We typically recommend a separate dev meter to avoid eating into committed production tokens.

Next step: I attached a proposed term sheet that includes the pilot concession (250k/mo for 3 months) and a sample DocuSign link if you want to proceed. Happy to jump on a brief call to walk through the worked example.

Attachments: Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference

From: Sylvia Kim <sylvia@paymentsinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anil Rao <anil@paymentsinc.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Hosted API commit / overage questions

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the worked example. A few follow-ups / negotiating points from our side: 

- Minimums: The 250k pilot looks fine, but procurement is pushing back on any annual lock for small customers. Can you make the pilot truly month-to-month for the three months (i.e., no annual commitment required to qualify)?
- Overage multiplier: 1.5x is higher than we expected. Can we get 1.25x for the first 3 months post-commit or a stepped overage (1.25x for first 1M over, then 1.5x)? We need to avoid big sticker shock if we have a traffic burst.
- Burst buffer: useful. Can we get one free 50% spike per month (not just first quarter)? We have intermittent big events and want predictable cost. Alternatively, if not feasible, can you agree to an explicit monthly cap on overage charges (e.g., no more than 150% of the committed monthly fee)?
- Pre-prod/dev: we will want dev traffic on a separate meter, but we need guidance on how to set that up in the Console so it doesn't count against commit.

Legal also asked for the exact formula you use to compute token billing for cached tokens that avoid generation — do you differentiate billed tokens (front tokens vs generation tokens) in the invoice? The example in the PDF was helpful but legal wants the explicit line they can put in the SOW.

If you can confirm the pilot month-to-month, a softened overage multiplier, and either a monthly burst event or an overage cap, we can move to signature. We’ll also route to our procurement lead (Anil) for review.

Thanks — Sylvia

--
Sylvia Kim
Head of Platform
Payments Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Kim <sylvia@paymentsinc.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Hosted API commit / overage questions

Hi Sylvia — appreciate the clear asks. I discussed options with RevOps and Product. Below is a commercial compromise we can sign off internally and route to legal/procurement: 

Commercial concession (Payments Inc. special):
- Pilot: 3-month pilot at 250k tokens/month, month-to-month (no annual lock required).
- Overage multiplier: 1.25x on commit per-token price for any overage during the pilot period. After pilot, standard 1.5x applies unless you elect to move to an annual commit tier (we'd reprice at that time).
- Burst: We will include one monthly free spike event up to 50% of committed tokens (i.e., up to +125k tokens for the 250k pilot) for the pilot term. Additional overage billed at the agreed multiplier.
- Overage cap alternative: If you'd prefer a cost cap instead, we can cap additional overage charges to 150% of the committed monthly fee for the pilot only. Please confirm which you prefer (free spike or cap).
- Pre-prod/dev: we'll provision a separate "dev" meter in your Console that is billed entirely on on-demand list rates (no commit). I attached a short setup guide and will have AE/SE provision the meter.
- Token billing: Invoiceable tokens = tokens billed after caching and prefix compression. Invoices include line items: committed tokens, used burst buffer, billed overage tokens, and effective per-token rates. I pasted the exact SOW language below for legal.

SOW language (suggested):
"Billed tokens are calculated on consumed tokens after automated prefix/KV caching and compression. The customer is billed for (a) committed tokens up to the committed volume; (b) consumed burst buffer tokens (if applicable); and (c) billed overage tokens at the agreed overage multiplier applied to the committed per-token rate. Billed tokens exclude tokens served from customer-side caching explicitly configured by the customer and documented in the Console settings."

Next steps:
- I uploaded a redline-ready term sheet and sample DocuSign envelope here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X2Y (DocuSign link inside).
- If you want the monthly cap instead of the single monthly spike, say so and I’ll include it in the term sheet.
- Rishi (cc) will review billing language for invoicing and create a HubSpot deal record with the concession flags.

If that works, we can route to Anil and Legal for signature.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
